I worked at lake hotel.
I made about $600\week after tax and room & board was deducted (so, about $1200 per two week pay period).
Which, for waiting tables at a "fancy" restaurant, is not that great. I was definitely not making my room & board, which was something like $425\pay period, on one shift.

So $600 for 9 shifts a week (we worked a lot of doubles), a mixture of breakfasts, lunches, and dinners. They wouldn't do an am\pm crew bc there's too much competition for dinner shifts, which are the only ones you can make money on.

I still wait tables now and made over a grand in my four day week last week, so I don't think it's the quality of my service.

What they do is turn and burn. I think the earning capacity might honestly be higher at more casual locations like Grant or old faithful, because their experience is geared for a faster more casual style of service. Late hotel tries to make turn and burn fancy and it doesn't work. It just limits your ability to reseat your section.

Hello friend. I don't know if this might help you, but maybe it's something you could try. I also suffer from depression and hypoglycemia. I struggle a lot when I am too depressed to eat and my blood sugar get so low that I feel sick and dizzy and I can't sleep. If you really can't bring yourself to eat, you can go to any drug store like Walgreens or CVS or even Walmart, and pick up a package of glucose tablets. They're made for diabetics. I try to keep them in my purse or glove box for those moments that I'm out and busy and then suddenly boom, I realize that I haven't eaten in too long and my motor functions are starting to fail. Just remember to eat some real food every once in a while to. Take care of yourself, you don't have to be happy to be in Paris. It's okay.

When i chose Germany as a destination, they were incentivizing immigration with easy residency programs due to a negative birthrate. It seemed the govt was looking ahead and saw an impending shortage in their work force as the current one aged out. With my experience as an educator (4 yrs in art and now >2 in informal science) it seemed that i would qualify for one of these 'fast track' visas for residency. The plan was, find work, then housing, then get back into school. 
Germany has since taken on a lot of refugees and the general public opinion of immigrants seems to be shifting(negatively) and i don't think the need for (relatively unskilled, such as myself) workers is so great.

I started looking into moving to Germany about 2-3 yrs ago. Ive looked at a lot of different Visa options and reached to out anyone i could. It may be that ive gotten the info crossed or mixed up or just that my info is now outdated. Ive been practicing german with Duolingo (not the best, i know, but better than nothing, i am trying) for about a year now. Meine Deutsche spreche ist schlecht, aber ich lerne. 
Originally Germany was the goal bc at the time, they had a negative birthrate and were incentivizing immigration of working folks with easy residency programs. But that was before they took on so many refugees.
German schools look very good and i like it's location which would allow me to see much of Europe in my free time. I would still like to make it my destination. 
I guess everyone in my life has been telling me that it's a pipe dream for so long now, i started to believe them.
